title: promote-release.mjs exits 1 on npm read lag after every write succeeds, skipping the GitHub Release and forcing a separate public repair
description:
Raised running the 0.13.0 latest-move (QCLI-433, DEC-169). scripts/promote-release.mjs moved every dist-tag successfully -- the six platforms and @opum-ai/quest all went latest -> 0.13.0 -- and then failed its OWN verification: "The writes returned success but the registry does not serve latest = 0.13.0 everywhere after 10 reads." It exited 1. npm reads lag npm writes (the runbook documents minutes), and the dist-tags settled shortly after: a re-read some minutes later showed latest 0.13.0 on all seven packages. The harm is not the exit code but what the exit SKIPS -- it happened BEFORE ensureGitHubRelease, so the GitHub Release v0.13.0 was never cut and had to be repaired out of band.

RUN OF RECORD: rollback record .claude/handovers/quest-cli-0.13.0-promote-record.json written 2026-10-07T14:51:03Z; promote exited 1; repair via node scripts/github-release.mjs --version 0.13.0 --create at about 14:55Z (exit 0).

DIRECTION: the README read-back (QCLI-400) already waits out lag and only WARNS; this dist-tag read-back should do the same rather than fail the run while the registry is still propagating a write it accepted. The fail-fast shape is also dangerous because it invites an operator to re-run the promote, which the runbook explicitly forbids on read lag (never re-publish or unpublish on it).

STEPS AFTER THE READ-BACK THAT DID NOT RUN, because it exited 1 there (recorded here as the concrete consequence; not a request to run them):
1. verifyFinalLauncher -- a deeper verification than the one that failed: that npm serves the qualified final/ launcher tarball as @opum-ai/quest@0.13.0, distinct from the verifyTags dist-tag check that timed out.
2. the success summary line: "Promoted: latest reads 0.13.0 on all 7 packages ..., and npm serves @opum-ai/quest@0.13.0 as the qualified opum-ai-quest-0.13.0.tgz. Rollback: --rollback <record>".
3. ensureGitHubRelease -- the release cut (now repaired manually, see above).
4. readBackReadme -- the README read-back (QCLI-399 AC3): reads the package-level readme and prints its byte count; when absent it only warns, with the ~25-minute lag note, and states not to roll back.
5. the final exit decision (process.exit(1) when the release cut did not succeed).

acceptanceCriteria.text: The dist-tag read-back in promote-release.mjs no longer exits 1 while the registry is still propagating a write it already accepted; it waits out the lag the way the README read-back does (QCLI-400) and then reports the settled verdict.

A run in which every write succeeds and the dist-tags settle to the promoted version runs to completion in ONE invocation -- ensureGitHubRelease, readBackReadme and the final exit decision all execute -- so no separate out-of-band GitHub Release repair is needed.

If the read-back still refuses after its lag window, its message names the reads it made, states that the writes returned success, and instructs the operator not to re-publish or unpublish, matching the README read-back wording.

implementationNotes:
MANUAL verifyFinalLauncher, 2026-10-07 — the step the 0.13.0 promote read-back skipped. Compared npm served @opum-ai/quest@0.13.0 against the qualified final/ launcher from run 37570426929 quest-candidate-bundle, by the same comparison bundle-integrity.mjs registryHoldsTarball makes (sha512- + base64(sha512(tarball)) against npm dist.integrity), with dist.shasum against sha1 as a second axis.
- npm serves: dist.integrity sha512-oUaVqtKmyWLMj4V6L0fDFb6PfwbT8tMzbA4wKeN483MT4nqSKfbY1tfFaqPvj3SjZdXYQaRmZ3pf4b+vXrKTdg== ; dist.shasum 5eb8ec5b05bf18fd673a8e44edce019b74dd28e6.
- Qualified final tarball final/opum-ai-quest-0.13.0.tgz (6514 bytes): sha512-base64 identical; sha1 5eb8ec5b05bf18fd673a8e44edce019b74dd28e6 identical.
Verdict: MATCH. So the timed-out exit skipped verifyFinalLauncher but left no gap in the published bytes — the launcher on latest is the qualified final launcher, byte for byte.

CROSS-REFERENCE: the lore-cli twin is LCLI-689 — "promote-latest.mjs fails the run on npm read lag after every write succeeded, so the GitHub Release is left uncut (paired with quest-cli QCLI-465)". LCLI-689 already names this record back. It reaches lore-cli dev via opum-ai/lore-cli PR #518 (branch chore/LCLI-665-promote-partial-state); as of this write that PR is open, so LCLI-689 sits on that branch, not on lore-cli dev. Fix the two promote scripts together — the wait-out-lag shape (as the README read-back, QCLI-400, already does) is the same change on each side.
